gold_assessment.reasoning: Gold: 5‑day history of cough and runny nose. Covered by generated hpi-001 and hpi-002, which state a continuous dry cough and runny nose for the past five to six days (minor variation in duration but same clinical content).
Gold: Dry cough keeping patient up at night. Covered by generated hpi-001 (dry cough) and hpi-003 (cough present throughout the day and disturbs her sleep at night).

Gold: Patient denies ear pain or sore throat. Generated ros-008 indicates no ear symptoms (aligned), but hpi-011 states intermittent sore throat attributed to coughing, which directly contradicts the denial of sore throat.

Gold: No shortness of breath or chest pain. Covered by hpi-005 (denies chest pain) and hpi-006 (denies day-to-day shortness of breath); ros-009 and ros-010 also restate these. Generated hpi-007/ros-011 add cough-induced/transient breathlessness but do not state baseline SOB.

Gold: Feeling tired, weak, and myalgia. Covered across hpi-008 (general tiredness), hpi-010 (muscle aches), ros-001 (tiredness), ros-003 (feeling weak/lethargic), ros-004/ros-017 (muscle aches/generalized muscle aches).

Gold: Feeling shivery, hot and cold, ?fever. Generated hpi-009 (chills with shivering especially at night) and ros-002 (chills) cover shivery/hot-cold symptoms; possible fever is only referenced later in plan-004/fu-002 as a symptom to monitor but the key symptom complex is captured.
Gold: No nausea/vomiting, appetite maintained. Covered by hpi-015 (no nausea or vomiting) and ros-013 (no nausea/vomiting), ros-014 (appetite maintained).
Gold: Initial diarrhea now resolved. Covered by hpi-013 (mild diarrhea at onset, resolved after a few days) and ros-012 (initial diarrhea resolved).
Gold: Nil urinary symptoms, no rashes. Covered by hpi-016 (no urinary issues), hpi-018 (no skin rash); also ros-015 (no urinary symptoms) and ros-016 (no skin rashes).
Gold: History of Type 2 diabetes and HTN. Covered by pmh-001 (type 2 diabetes mellitus) and pmh-002 (hypertension), and repeated in asm-006 and asm-007.
Gold: Takes metformin and lisinopril. Covered by med-001 (Metformin) and med-002 (Lisinopril).
Gold: NKDA. Covered by allergy-001 (no known drug allergies).
Gold: Father has Type 2 diabetes. Covered by fh-001 (father with type 2 diabetes).
Gold: Lives with partner, works in IT, denies stress. Covered for living with partner (sfh-001) and working in IT (sfh-003). No generated fact reflects ‘denies stress,’ so that portion is omitted.
Gold: Ex-smoker, stopped 6 months ago. Covered by sfh-005 (quit six months ago) and sfh-006 (no current tobacco use; quit six months ago).

Gold: Drinks <9 units/week. Generated sfh-007: 2–3 glasses of wine up to three evenings/week. Depending on glass size, this can exceed 9 units, and the documentation explicitly quantifies a higher, not-bounded-as-<9 intake; therefore it conflicts with the stated maximum in gold.
Gold: Impression viral URTI. Covered by asm-001 (acute URTI probable viral) and asm-002 (viral URTI most likely).
Gold: Supportive management – bed rest, fluids, regular paracetamol. Covered by plan-001 (rest), plan-002 (adequate hydration), and med-003/plan-003 (regular Paracetamol).

Gold: Review in 5–7 days if not better. Generated plan-005 and fu-001 specify return if not improving in 2–3 days, which is a different and earlier timeframe, thus conflicting with the gold follow-up interval.

Gold: Seek earlier review for worsening symptoms (fever, SOB, chest pain). Covered by plan-004 and fu-002 which instruct return sooner with new concerning symptoms including fever, shortness of breath, chest pain.
